editorial:
Ray Dennis Steckler directed and produced this horror musical in the US, releasing it on February 10, 1964 through Fairway International Pictures. He shot it for about $38,000 at a Masonic temple in Glendale, California, and also starred in it under the name Cash Flagg. Vilmos Zsigmond, who later won an Academy Award, worked on the cinematography. Creators come to it for its cult reputation, its carnival-and-zombie imagery and its musical numbers.

The rights question is the 1964 copyright. A film from that year is free only if it was published without a valid notice or its registration was never renewed in the 1991–1993 window. This dossier did not confirm either. The Internet Archive uploads carry a public-domain label, but that label comes from the uploader, not from a copyright record. Check the Copyright Office public records and the Catalog of Copyright Entries renewal volumes before relying on any copy. The score by André Brummer and Libby Quinn and the screenplay credits should be checked as part of the same search.
faq: Is this film in the public domain?

Not confirmed. The queue suggests the 1964 copyright may not have been renewed, but this review found no primary renewal-absence record. Search the Copyright Office catalog and the Catalog of Copyright Entries renewal volumes yourself before reuse.
Does the Internet Archive's public-domain label settle it?
No. The label was applied by the uploader and is not a copyright record. Use it as a lead, and confirm the renewal status independently.
